newsitem.title: CANADA: Harbour sells Alberta gas field stake.
newsitem.headline: Harbour sells Alberta gas field stake.

text.p: Harbour Petroleum Co Ltd said on Monday it sold its 100 percent interest in the Jenner and Cessford gas fields in eastern Alberta for C$29.5 million.
Harbour said it would record a C$11.9 million gain on the sale of the properties.
The company purchased Jenner for C$16.8 million two years ago and upgraded its production by drilling 55 new wells, which were financed through the use of an operating lease on the gas compressors.
The sale, still subject to shareholder approval, would allow the company to reduce its debt to zero and use C$10 million cash on hand to fund 1997 capital spending.
Harbour said it developed and exploration and development drilling program of high-reward prospects in central Alberta and the Peace River Arch.
It also said it intensified its evaluation activity for potential asset acquisitions.

"This is an imprortant new phase for Harbour, as after this sale of Jenner the company's average daily production will be approximately 700 (barrels of oil equivalent)...and the first goal will be to make large additions to our reserve base in the near term," it said.
